key_pathways: Renal tubular secretion via organic anion transporter (OAT)

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Licorice causes sodium retention and potassium depletion, counteracting furosemide's diuretic effect and exacerbating hypokalemia
avoid_supplements.action: Advise patient to avoid licorice and licorice-containing products; monitor serum potassium and sodium levels closely

avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Furosemide causes significant potassium wasting; excessive supplementation may lead to overcorrection if dose is adjusted, but deficiency risk is primary concern requiring balanced monitoring
avoid_supplements.action: Do not supplement without serum potassium monitoring; coordinate supplementation with prescriber based on lab values

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (including supplements containing willow bark, meadowsweet)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal perfusion and decrease furosemide efficacy; increase risk of acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid NSAIDs; use acetaminophen or other alternatives; monitor renal function and potassium if concurrent use unavoidable

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild diuretic properties and could enhance furosemide effect unpredictably
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure and electrolytes if used concurrently

caution_supplements.name: Hawthorn
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have diuretic and cardiovascular effects that could potentiate furosemide
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure and symptoms of volume depletion

avoid_foods.name: High-sodium processed foods, salt-cured meats, canned soups
avoid_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium intake counteracts the blood pressure-lowering and fluid-reducing effects of furosemide
avoid_foods.action: Recommend sodium restriction (<2g/day); educate on reading food labels and avoiding processed foods

caution_foods.name: High-potassium foods (bananas, spinach, orange juice, avocado, sweet potatoes)
caution_foods.mechanism: Furosemide causes potassium depletion; while normal dietary potassium is beneficial, excessive intake requires monitoring in context of serum potassium levels
caution_foods.action: Include moderate potassium-rich foods in diet; adjust based on serum potassium monitoring and prescriber recommendation

caution_foods.name: Licorice-containing candies and herbal teas
caution_foods.mechanism: Minor exposure may have minimal effect, but regular consumption compounds sodium retention and potassium loss
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; educate patient on potential effects

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum electrolytes (potassium, sodium, magnesium, calcium), renal function (BUN/creatinine), blood pressure, and fluid status regularly. Particular attention to hypokalemia risk, especially in patients on concurrent ACE inhibitors or on potassium supplementation.
